findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought trailed SPY by 0.67% on average (69 buys, 42% of them ahead of SPY; t = -1.2, within noise).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.84%, so selling gave that up (143 sells; t = -2.4, significant at 5%).

Decision IC: on the 40 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of -0.040 with the next five days' returns (IC IR -0.33, t = -2.1, significant at 5%).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 43 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.003 with the next five days' returns (t = 0.1, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.37 (t 7.3), size 0.02 (t 0.6), growth -0.47 (t -8.0), momentum 0.07 (t 4.2); together they explain 40% of the daily variation (R²).
Of the +3.6% a year it earned over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +4.0%, momentum -1.7%, growth -1.1%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is +2.4% a year (t = 0.4, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for +1.2% a year of it, and the +2.4% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
P&L: +$6,181 in all, +$4,622 from 62 positions and +$1,559 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$7,603, 8 positions); 3-5 days the least (-$6,823, 19 positions).
By sector: Industrials made the most (+$5,099, 8 positions); Technology the least (-$2,626, 10 positions).
By stock: UNP made the most (+$2,917, 2 positions); AMD the least (-$3,152, 2 positions).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 96 days -3.3% (SPY +2.0%); neutral 18 days -0.5% (SPY +4.5%); uncertain 97 days +9.5% (SPY +4.8%); risk-off 6 days +0.7% (SPY +0.3%).
News: 18 positions opened on news made +$6,235, the other 44 -$1,612; 11 positions closed on news made -$897; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 0.06% (t 0.0).

Concentration: the gains are spread out (the best two positions made 16% of them) but winners and losers nearly cancel, so the best two made 73% of the net P&L; the best was UNP bought 2026-04-16 and sold 2026-09-01, +$1,820. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +4.4% instead of +6.2%.

holdings.score: the weights it held after each decision (0 for stocks not held)
